raw_segments.text: Enneas, the priest and king with laurel crowned, his hoary locks with purple filace bound, who
saw my sire the Delian sure ascend, came forth with eager haste to meet his friend, invites
him to his palace, and in sign of ancient love their plighted hands they join.
Then to the temple of the god I went, and thus before the shrine my vows present.
Give O Thembrius give a resting place to the sad relics of the Trojan race, a seat secure,
a region of their own, a lasting empire, and a happier town.
Where shall we fix? Where shall our labors end? Whom shall we follow and what fate attend?
Let not my prayers a doubtful answer find, but in clear auguries unveil thy mind.
Scarce had I said. He shook the holy ground, the laurels, and the lofty hills around,
and from the tripos rushed a bellowing sound. Prostrate we fell, confess the present god,
who gave this answer from his dark abode. Undaunted youths, go seek that mother earth
from which your ancestors derive their birth. The soil that sent you forth, her ancient
race and her old bosom shall again embrace. Through the wide world th, enyen house shall
reign, and children's children shall the crown sustain. Thus Phoebus did our future
fates disclose, a mighty tumult mixed with joy arose.
